# TestQuery

Test Query (tq) is a command line tool to query Go test results with a SQL interface.

This tool was designed to make extracting information from tests easier for the average developer (as long as you know SQL of course - but everyone should learn SQL anyway ^^).

web.title: SQL Online Test
web.description:
# SQL Online Test
## About the test
- Writing queries and subqueries that join, group, filter, and aggregate data.

## Sample public questions
Write a query that returns, for each user who has more than one session:

```
TABLE users
  id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  userName VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL

TABLE roles
  id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  role VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
```

Write a query that select all distinct pet names.

```sql
SELECT users.name, COUNT(friends.user1) as count FROM users
LEFT JOIN friends
ON users.id = friends.user1 OR users.id = friends.user2
WHERE users.sex = 'f'
GROUP BY users.id, users.name;
```

web.title: To Test SQL Queries
web.description:
### To Test SQL Queries
![](https://portal.rfgen.com/help/6.0/RFgen6_Help/Content/Resources/Images/SQL/SQL-QueryTab.png)

To access this function click on **Testing > SQL Queries**.

![](https://portal.rfgen.com/help/6.0/RFgen6_Help/Content/Resources/Images/SQL/SQL-Log-ERP-Toggle.png)

The same screen is also used to preserve and recall the statements from **SQL History**. This utility can also be used to undo updates, check results, delete values or even adding and dropping tables. Any SQL command entered here is submitted to the ODBC driver for execution.

**Maximum Rows: 1000** utility allows you to change the 1000 maximum row default to a different row value.

The connection is controlled by a toggle button that you slide to enable or disable the ERP connection.

To test the query, enable the ERP mode (slide box to the right), enter your statement in the query box and press Execute. The execution will display results in the second box.

The SQL Query Window gives a current snapshot of the data in your database. As transactions are applied against your data, you will need to re-execute your SQL statement.

If the intent is “select * from TableName”, then only specifying the table name will default to the “select * from” when executed.

The multi-line text box allows the entry of several SQL statements. In this case, highlight the intended SQL statement and click Execute from the menu.

Multiple SQL statements must be separated by semi-colons “;” .

`Select * from items;
`

`Select * from itemmaster;
`

If no text is highlighted, then it will look at the current insertion point to determine with SQL statement to execute based upon semi-colon delimiters.

Most generic queries can be entered and executed for any brand of SQL. For example, if you entered:

SELECT TOP 10 * FROM T001L; = Microsoft SQL. SELECT * FROM T001L WHERE ROWNUM <= 10;
